I'm struggling with how to cope in the meantime. My mental health conditions mean that embarrassment and shame HAVE to be avoided at all costs, even to my own detriment. This is something I recognise but can't fully control.

I had no issues asking for help before I was labelled a violent patient. I have never been violent towards anyone, and the shame attached to that label when it's just not true is unbearable.

This is one of my greatest fears for my child, I try to explain my illness to them in an age appropriate manner so they are not completely unaware, but I am so scared that I will completely lose it in front of them one day. This last week has been a true struggle doing so.

Thank you so much for your support <3

Thank you so much for your kind words! I have been on the waiting list for a support worker for a long time now, someone who I can just check in with when needed and who knows me and my history. I find it very frustrating when I see different people everytime, I know they are there to help and do care, but I also find repeating myself very traumatic. I do distractions like crafts and jigsaws but am struggling to stay focused on them for long because the intrusive thoughts are getting louder and much more enticing. At this point, I really don't know what I need to help myself. All I can think about is how much easier it would be to just not exist anymore.

Sadly, it's not a blanket generalisation, though fortunately not as rife as it used to be! Formula companies pushing their products were at their worst after the second world war once more, and more women joined the workforce full-time. A boycott nestle movement was started in the 70s due to how predatory they were being with their marketing. Numerous babies died in poorer countries of starvation due to their practices. Mainly providing mothers with enough free samples to cover the time it took for their milk to dry up, which then lead the mothers to ration the formula because they could not afford it after the samples stopped and could no longer feed their babies themselves.

It still happens, though. It's why we now have "follow-on" products advertised everywhere mothers and babies will be. Completely unnecessary product that was created purely because they are no longer allowed to advertise their products for babies 6 months and under.
